text: Two kyu. I have the book with me if you want to see the standard sequence. I always have the book with me.
Nadia Ferreira, two kyu, fourth year. I sit in on the beginners' classes and I am not embarrassed about it.
Hana taught me corner-side-centre in this room eleven years ago and I still count it out on my fingers in real games.
That is not a confession. That is the advice.
I will give you stones. As many as it takes to make it a real game -- there is no dignity in a close loss.
The book will still be here. So, unfortunately, will page forty.
You beat me with fewer stones than last time. That is the only measurement that means anything and you should write it down.
Brandt sent you. She sends everybody, and she has never once sent them for the right reason.
Here. Take it -- the whole thing, not a photocopy of page forty, because page forty on its own is where people go wrong.
I want it back before the exam. Not because I will read it. Because I will want to be holding it.
You still have it. Good -- that means you have not finished with it, which is the correct state to be in.
Page forty is the one she means. It is even. I have never once got an even corner out of it.
You beat her.
She will have told you it was not the book. She is right, and she will still tell you to read the first forty pages of the next one.
Which page was it?
No -- do not answer. It was not a page. It never is, and I have six books and eleven years of knowing that and I still ask.
Thank you for bringing it back. Most of them do not.
Keep it. I know where you sit.
It is back on the shelf where I can see it, which is what it is for.
Brandt has started telling people to read the first forty pages of the endgame one. I am not lending that one out.
